title: Screenshot tooling: general frame-to-bounds route, crop and scale, image diff, multiview for mesh-viewer
description: Framing one overlay for a screenshot took an agent eight calls of orbit guessing, ring close-ups framed the wrong spot because orbit-set has no target, screenshot inspection needed crop-and-upscale round trips with an uninstalled PIL, and image comparison fell back to sha256sum (report items 19, 23, 27). Add a general frame route: fit the camera to a bounding box given explicitly or derived from a named selection (an edge-mark set, an overlay, a patch id, a tag, a ring id), with a padding fraction; orbit-set gains a target point. screenshot accepts an optional crop region and integer scale so a two-pixel ring line can be inspected without extra tooling. ixdar-cli image-diff a.png b.png prints RMSE and the count of pixels differing beyond a fuzz, using only the standard library or a dependency added to the CLI's pyproject. Make ixdar-cli multiview render mesh-viewer content instead of black (MESH-53; mark it DONE when this lands). gen-docs and test_cli.py updated.
definition-of-done: 1. frame --selection ring:1 on the fertility ring fixture centres and fills the ring in the screenshot. 2. screenshot with a crop and scale returns the enlarged region. 3. image-diff on two screenshots that differ only by a ring reports a small non-zero pixel count and zero for identical images. 4. multiview on mesh-viewer shows the mesh in all views. 5. Docs regenerated, tests green, screenshots under tmp/.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: bounds computation for each selection kind; image-diff on synthetic images. 2. Manual: the four DoD screenshots on fertility, attached under tmp/ and named in changes-made.
unknowns: The DoD names dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl and a ring:1 selection kind, and neither exists on master: there is no fertility_rings.dsl anywhere on disk or in git history, and no ring concept in the runtime (every ring hit is a 1-ring vertex neighbourhood, a patch-boundary walk, or the numeric rings= parameter of uv_sphere/mesh_disk). Both appear to come from the CRAW ring tool, which is still unlanded in the craw-22 and craw-23 worktrees. I verified DoD 1 on the closest real equivalent, an edge-mark loop on fixtures/torus_tighten_loop: frame --selection edge-mark:b_tightened_loop centres and fills the torus meridian (tmp/tool7-frame-edgemark.png). Ruling needed: is that substitution acceptable, or should a ring: selection kind be added to SelectionBounds when the ring tool lands? Same question for MESH-53, whose DoD also names that fixture; I verified eight non-black views on skull.dsl and on the torus fixture instead.

DoD 3 asks for two screenshots that differ only by a ring. In the live scene the edge-mark overlay persists across a mesh-dsl reload (applyEdgeMarkOverlay returns early when the new bundle has no marks), so I could not produce that exact pair without a code change I judged out of scope. Verified instead: identical screenshots report zero, a small localized change reports 424 pixels, and the synthetic 12-pixel ring case is a unit test. Say if you want the overlay cleared on a reload with no marks.
changes-made: MESH-53 root cause and fix: MultiviewScreenshot.java built the 4x2 composite BufferedImage and wrote it straight to disk without ever drawing the eight captures into it, so every multiview PNG was black regardless of scene or timing. Added the Graphics2D drawImage loop plus the shadowed white view labels (the java.awt Color/Font imports the file already carried, wrongly pointing at ixdar.graphics.render classes). Verified: multiview on mesh-viewer now returns blankViews 0, meanChannelValue 48.6, and all eight labelled views show the mesh (tmp/tool7-multiview.png, 4096x2048).

New route POST /ui/frame (ixdar-cli frame) in ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/platform/automation/endpoints/ui/Frame.java: fits the orbit camera to a bounding box from --selection or an explicit --bounds minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ, with --padding as a fraction of the fitted radius and optional --azimuth/--elevation (current angles kept otherwise). Distance solves radius/sin(half-FOV) against the narrower of the vertical and horizontal view angles, and setDistanceBounds is widened first so OrbitMouseTrap does not clamp a close-up fit away.

SelectionBounds.java resolves kind:name to an axis-aligned box over whatever the viewer holds: tag:NAME (per-vertex _tags mask), edge-mark:LABEL (per-edge-id _edge_marks flags, both endpoints), patch:ID (decomposer patch dense vertex indices), mesh and overlay. A bare name is tried as tag, then edge-mark, then patch id, and a miss lists the names that do exist. Verified on the running scene: frame --selection edge-mark:b_tightened_loop on fixtures/torus_tighten_loop matched 96 vertices, centre 1.0,0.0,0.0 radius 0.495 (analytically correct for a 0.35 minor-radius meridian) and the close-up fills the frame (tmp/tool7-frame-edgemark.png); patch:3 matched 34 vertices and framed the eye socket (tmp/tool7-frame-patch3.png); an explicit crown box centred within 2 percent of the predicted screen position (tmp/tool7-frame-crown.png); tag:cranium and overlay both resolve.

MeshNodeViewerScene gained the three accessors the resolver needs: getOverlayMesh() with a new overlayMesh field set in loadOverlay and cleared in disposeOverlay, getGeometryBundle() returning the mesh-file bundle or the DSL graph's final geometry output, and decomposePatches() exposing the cached decomposition.

screenshot gained --crop x,y,width,height (pixels from the top-left, clamped) and --scale N (integer nearest-neighbour, so a two-pixel line stays crisp). Response now carries width/height of the written file plus framebufferWidth/framebufferHeight, scale and crop. Verified: --crop 340,430,140,140 --scale 6 wrote an 840x840 PNG of the eye-socket rim (tmp/tool7-crop-eye.png).

orbit-set gained --target x,y,z (OrbitMouseTrap.setTarget), which is what made ring close-ups frame the wrong spot; orbit-get now reports target as well. Verified: orbit-get after frame --selection patch:3 reports target 0.690,0.387,0.713, exactly the selection centre.

ixdar-cli image-diff FIRST SECOND (positional) prints RMSE, differing pixel count and fraction, max channel delta and an identical flag, with --fuzz (default 8) and --max-differing to fail on regression. ixdar-cli image-stats IMAGE reports mean, min and max channel values and a blank flag, exiting 6 on a single-colour frame or below --min-mean. Both use a new standard-library PNG decoder, ixdar_automation_cli/png_image.py (8-bit, colour types 0/2/3/4/6, all five row filters); no dependency was added to pyproject. Measured: identical 1024x1024 screenshots give rmse 0.0 and 0 differing pixels; a 0.003 rad orbit nudge gives 424 differing pixels (0.04 percent), rmse 0.41, in 1.06 s; a full 4096x2048 multiview diff takes 1.82 s.

cli_registry.py and ixdar_cli.py gained positional-parameter support (CliOption(positional=True)) so image-diff reads as the review item wrote it, image-diff a.png b.png, rather than as two flags. Additive: every existing command keeps its flags.

Seven tests added to ixdar_automation_cli/test_cli.py: PNG decode agreement across two row filters, image-diff zero for identical and 12 differing pixels for a synthetic 12-pixel ring, --max-differing gating, size-mismatch rejection, the MESH-53 black-frame check on a synthetic black PNG, positional parsing, and a manifest check that screenshot exposes crop/scale, orbit-set exposes target, and frame exists with its five flags. 40 tests green; mvn -q compile -pl annotations,ixdar-app exits 0 checkstyle-clean; ixdar-cli gen-docs reports no drift.
